subject: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?

messages.author: 8d4cd0b2463d6bd3
messages.subject: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?
parts:
Hi,

What is an acceptable number of different random seeds to use with irace?  I guess it depends on how many experiments are run in irace and how many different parameters there are to tune, but an approximate number or formula would be useful.

Daniel

messages.author: 8d4cd0b2463d6bd3
messages.subject: Re: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?
parts:
Hi Manuel,

What I mean is that it is possible to set the seed for irace each time irace is run, rather than accepting the randomly generated seed, so that a run is repeatable.  I provide a seed as a command line argument to irace, for example:
$ IRACE_HOME/bin/irace --seed 130932630

What I am asking is: how many times (each time with a different seed) should I run irace to get a good sample of the parameters that are being tuned?

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?
parts:
I understand now. That is as difficult to answer as how many runs you need to get a good estimation of the mean performance of any stochastic algorithm: It depends. We usually do 25 or 30 runs as a rule of thumb for comparing different irace variants. But if my goal was to find very good configurations, and I don't care about estimating irace's average performance, then I would probably increase the budget of each run and reduce the number of runs to 5 or 10.  If one has little total budget and a large parameter space, it may be better to do one long run than many short ones. I don't think there is an easy answer available at the moment.

Cheers,

Manuel.
